title: What a commit message is for
summary: A commit message is a note to a future reader: your teammate, the person fixing a bug at 2 a.m., or you in six months. There is a simple format that every team recognises.

sections.heading: Headline first
sections.body:
The first line is a headline. Tools show it on its own everywhere: in the log, on pull requests, in release notes. Keep it short (aim for 50 characters, never more than 72), and write it as an instruction: `Add salt to pancake recipe`, not `added salt` or `Salt.`

A quick test: the headline should complete the sentence "If applied, this commit will ...".

sections.heading: Blank line, then the why
sections.body:
If the headline is not enough, leave one empty line and write a short paragraph. Do not repeat what the diff shows; explain what the reader cannot see: the reason, the trade-off, the ticket or incident it relates to.

Example:

`Raise oven to 220 degrees for a crisp crust`

`At 180 the loaf came out pale and soft. 220 for the first 20 minutes gives the crust we wanted.`

sections.heading: One change per commit
sections.body: A message is easy to write when the commit does one thing. If you find yourself writing "and" in a headline, that is often two commits. The staging area (previous lesson) is how you split them.

takeaways: Short imperative headline, under 72 characters, no full stop.
Blank line, then the reason, if the headline is not enough.
One change per commit makes messages easy.

quiz.question: Which headline follows the convention?
options: Fix login timeout on slow networks
quiz.explanation: Imperative, specific, no trailing full stop.

quiz.question: What goes in the body of a message?
options: A copy of the changed lines
quiz.explanation: The diff already shows what; the body explains why. Git adds your name automatically.

quiz.question: Your headline reads 'Add salt and fix typo and update notes'. What should you do?
options: Split the work into separate commits
quiz.explanation: Several unrelated changes belong in several commits.
